editorial:
Imagine a world where a scientist thinks he is a god, but ends up creating his own worst nightmare. You get to follow Victor Frankenstein, a man who is way too proud of his own brain, as he stitches together a living being from dead parts. The vibe is dark and moody, but it feels more like a sad family story than just a scary monster flick. You will feel for the creature because he just wants to be loved, while Victor is too scared and mean to give him a chance. It is a wild ride that asks if being a parent is about blood or how you treat someone.

What really hits home is the acting, as the chemistry between the creator and the monster is intense and heartbreaking. The pacing is steady, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you are looking for non-stop jumpscares. If you love stories about monsters with hearts of gold, you need to see this. For the best experience, you should stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the cool makeup details, or just grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection so you own it forever.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the monster tracks Victor to the frozen north to force him to make a female partner. Victor destroys the second creature instead, which makes the monster snap. They have a huge fight where Victor is eventually killed by his own creation. Feeling completely alone and full of regret, the monster sets himself on fire and walks into the ice to die, ending the cycle of pain for both of them.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark fairy tales and emotional stories about outcasts.
